ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Nocturnal reflux

A patient with nighttime reflux eats a large meal immediately before bed and then lies flat. He asks about a practical behavior change to complement prescribed treatment. Which recommendation most directly addresses this pattern?

  1. Eat the largest meal just before sleep
  2. Lie flat immediately after eating
  3. Use extra pillows only to flex the neck as a guaranteed cure
  4. Increase every meal size to improve lower sphincter tone
  5. Avoid meals shortly before bedtime and consider head-of-bed elevation
Answer and explanation

Avoid meals shortly before bedtime and consider head-of-bed elevation

Meal timing and positioning can reduce nocturnal reflux.

Option explanations

Avoid meals shortly before bedtime and consider head-of-bed elevation: Meal timing and positioning can reduce nocturnal reflux.

Eat the largest meal just before sleep: This may aggravate nighttime symptoms.

Lie flat immediately after eating: Recumbency can worsen reflux.

Use extra pillows only to flex the neck as a guaranteed cure: Neck flexion is not equivalent to effective head-of-bed elevation and cannot guarantee control.

Increase every meal size to improve lower sphincter tone: Large meals may increase reflux.
